results.title: Normal covering number of the symmetric group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the normal covering number $\gamma(S_n)$ is the least $k$ for which there are proper subgroups $H_1, \dots, H_k$ of the symmetric group $S_n$ such that every element of $S_n$ is conjugate to an element of some $H_i$. When no such subgroups exist, as for $n \le 2$, it is $0$.

results.title: Bubboloni–Praeger–Spiga conjectured value
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n \ge 2$, write $n = p_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots p_r^{\alpha_r}$ with primes $p_1 < \cdots < p_r$ and exponents $\alpha_i \ge 1$, and let $p_2$ be the least prime factor of $n / p_1^{\alpha_1}$. The conjectured value of $n$ is the rational number $\frac{n}{2}(1 - \frac{1}{p_1})$ if $r = 1$ and $\alpha_1 = 1$; $\frac{n}{2}(1 - \frac{1}{p_1}) + 1$ if $r = 1$ and $\alpha_1 \ge 2$;…

results.title: Bubboloni–Praeger–Spiga normal covering conjecture (eventual form)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: There is a natural number $N$ such that, for every $n \ge N$, the normal covering number $\gamma(S_n)$ of the symmetric group $S_n$ equals the Bubboloni–Praeger–Spiga conjectured value of $n$.

results.title: Refutation of the Bubboloni–Praeger–Spiga normal covering conjecture
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: It is not the case that there is a natural number $N$ such that, for every $n \ge N$, the normal covering number $\gamma(S_n)$ of the symmetric group $S_n$ equals the Bubboloni–Praeger–Spiga conjectured value of $n$. In other words, the conjecture fails for arbitrarily large $n$.

results.title: Conjugate subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ and an element $x \in G$, the conjugate subgroup is $A^x = x^{-1} A x = \{x^{-1} a x : a \in A\}$.

results.title: Paranormal subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ is paranormal (Z. I. Borevich) when, for every $x \in G$, the conjugate $A^x = x^{-1} A x$ is contained in the subgroup generated by the conjugates $A^u$ with $u$ in the subgroup $\langle A, A^x \rangle$ generated by $A$ and $A^x$.

results.title: Polynormal subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ is polynormal (Z. I. Borevich) when, for every $x \in G$, the conjugate $A^x = x^{-1} A x$ is contained in the subgroup generated by the conjugates $A^u$ with $u \in A^{\langle x \rangle}$, where $A^{\langle x \rangle}$ is the subgroup generated by the conjugates $A^{x^n}$ with $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Polynormal subgroups of finite groups are paranormal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Kourovka 14.50 (Z. I. Borevich; A. S. Kondratiev): every polynormal subgroup of a finite group is paranormal.

results.title: A polynormal subgroup that is not paranormal (Kourovka 14.50 refuted)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a finite group $G$ with a subgroup $A$ that is polynormal but not paranormal. So the conjecture of Kourovka Problem 14.50 is false.

results.title: Generalized Sylvester sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the generalized Sylvester sequence $(s_k(n))_{k \ge 0}$ is the sequence of natural numbers defined by $s_0(n) = n + 1$ and $s_{k+1}(n) = s_k(n)^2 - s_k(n) + 1$ for $k \ge 0$.

results.title: Initial term of the generalized Sylvester sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the generalized Sylvester sequence $(s_k(n))_{k \ge 0}$ satisfies $s_0(n) = n + 1$.

results.title: Recurrence for the generalized Sylvester sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the generalized Sylvester sequence $(s_k(n))_{k \ge 0}$ satisfies $s_{k+1}(n) = s_k(n)^2 - s_k(n) + 1$.

results.title: Positivity of the generalized Sylvester sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the term $s_k(n)$ of the generalized Sylvester sequence is positive.

results.title: Sylvester numbers
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The Sylvester numbers $S_0, S_1, S_2, \dots$ are the natural numbers given by $S_0 = 2$ and $S_{n+1} = S_n^2 - S_n + 1$ for $n \ge 0$, so the sequence begins $2, 3, 7, 43, 1807, \dots$. It is the generalized Sylvester sequence with parameter $1$.

results.title: Divisibility of differences of Sylvester numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(S_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Sylvester sequence, $S_0 = 2$ and $S_{n+1} = S_n^2 - S_n + 1$. For all natural numbers $k$, $m$ and $n$ with $k \ge 1$, $m \ge k$ and $n \ge k$, the integer $(S_k - 1)^2$ divides $S_n - S_m$.

results.title: Sylvester numbers modulo 4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(S_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Sylvester sequence, $S_0 = 2$ and $S_{n+1} = S_n^2 - S_n + 1$. For every $n \ge 1$, $S_n \equiv 3 \pmod 4$.

results.title: Sylvester numbers modulo 36
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(S_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Sylvester sequence, $S_0 = 2$ and $S_{n+1} = S_n^2 - S_n + 1$. For every $n \ge 2$, $S_n \equiv 7 \pmod{36}$.

results.title: Sylvester numbers modulo 1764
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(S_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Sylvester sequence, $S_0 = 2$ and $S_{n+1} = S_n^2 - S_n + 1$. For every $n \ge 3$, $S_n \equiv 43 \pmod{1764}$.

results.title: Alternating divisibility for Sylvester numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(S_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Sylvester sequence, $S_0 = 2$ and $S_{n+1} = S_n^2 - S_n + 1$. For all natural numbers $k$ and $n$ with $1 \le k \le n$, the integer $S_k^2 + 1$ divides the integer $S_n - (-1)^{n-k} S_k$.

results.title: Sylvester numbers of even index modulo 10
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(S_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Sylvester sequence, $S_0 = 2$ and $S_{n+1} = S_n^2 - S_n + 1$. For every $i \ge 1$, $S_{2i} \equiv 7 \pmod{10}$.

results.title: Sylvester numbers of odd index modulo 10
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(S_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Sylvester sequence, $S_0 = 2$ and $S_{n+1} = S_n^2 - S_n + 1$. For every $i \ge 1$, $S_{2i+1} \equiv 3 \pmod{10}$.

results.title: Mersenne numbers in the Sylvester sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(S_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Sylvester sequence, $S_0 = 2$ and $S_{n+1} = S_n^2 - S_n + 1$. The natural numbers $x$ such that $x = S_n$ for some $n$ and $x = 2^r - 1$ for some $r \ge 1$ are exactly $3$ and $7$.

results.title: The only triangular Sylvester number is $3$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S_n$ denote the $n$-th Sylvester number. A natural number $x$ equals $S_n$ for some $n$ and satisfies $2x = m(m + 1)$ for some natural number $m \ge 1$ if and only if $x = 3$.

results.title: No Sylvester number is perfect
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the $n$-th Sylvester number $S_n$ is not a perfect number.

results.title: Prime divisors congruent to 3 modulo 4 of Sylvester numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(S_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Sylvester sequence, $S_0 = 2$ and $S_{n+1} = S_n^2 - S_n + 1$. For every $n \ge 1$, $S_n$ has a prime divisor $p$ with $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$.

results.title: Sylvester numbers are not perfect powers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(S_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Sylvester sequence, $S_0 = 2$ and $S_{n+1} = S_n^2 - S_n + 1$. For every $n$ there are no natural numbers $a \ge 2$ and $m \ge 2$ with $S_n = a^m$.

results.title: Sylvester numbers next to perfect powers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(S_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Sylvester sequence, $S_0 = 2$ and $S_{n+1} = S_n^2 - S_n + 1$. For every $n$ other than $1$ and $2$ there are no natural numbers $a \ge 2$ and $m \ge 2$ with $S_n = a^m + 1$ or $S_n = a^m - 1$.

results.title: Coprime solutions of $x^2 + 3 = 4y^n$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $x$ and $y$, the conditions $n \ge 3$, $x \ge 1$, $y \ge 1$, $\gcd(x, y) = 1$ and $x^2 + 3 = 4y^n$ hold if and only if $n \ge 3$ and either $x = y = 1$ or $(n, x, y) = (3, 37, 7)$ (Luca–Tengely–Togbé).

results.title: Coprime solutions of $x^2 + 7 = 4y^n$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $x$ and $y$, the conditions $n \ge 3$, $x \ge 1$, $y \ge 1$, $\gcd(x, y) = 1$ and $x^2 + 7 = 4y^n$ hold if and only if $(n, x, y)$ is $(3, 5, 2)$, $(5, 11, 2)$ or $(13, 181, 2)$ (Luca–Tengely–Togbé).

results.title: Coordinate map of a Weierstrass variable change
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a variable change $C = (u, r, s, t)$ over a field $F$, with $u \in F^\times$ and $r, s, t \in F$, the affine coordinate map of $C$ sends $(x, y) \in F^2$ to $(u^2 x + r,\ u^3 y + u^2 s x + t)$.

results.title: Variable changes act bijectively on affine coordinates
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a variable change $C = (u, r, s, t)$ over a field $F$, the map $(x, y) \mapsto (u^2 x + r,\ u^3 y + u^2 s x + t)$ is a bijection $F^2 \to F^2$, whose inverse is the corresponding map of the inverse variable change $C^{-1}$.

results.title: Variable changes transform the Weierstrass equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over a field $F$, let $C = (u, r, s, t)$ be a variable change and let $C \cdot W$ be the transformed curve. A pair $(x, y) \in F^2$ satisfies the Weierstrass equation of $C \cdot W$ if and only if $(u^2 x + r,\ u^3 y + u^2 s x + t)$ satisfies the Weierstrass equation of $W$.

results.title: Variable changes biject affine solutions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over a field $F$, let $C = (u, r, s, t)$ be a variable change and let $C \cdot W$ be the transformed curve. The map $(x, y) \mapsto (u^2 x + r,\ u^3 y + u^2 s x + t)$ is a bijection from the solutions $(x, y) \in F^2$ of the Weierstrass equation of $C \cdot W$ onto the solutions in $F^2$ of the Weierstrass equation of $W$; its inverse is the corresponding map of $C^{-1}$.

results.title: Variable changes biject rational points
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $W$ be an elliptic Weierstrass curve over a field $F$, let $C = (u, r, s, t)$ be a variable change and let $C \cdot W$ be the transformed curve. There is a bijection from the rational points of $C \cdot W$ to the rational points of $W$, where in both cases the point at infinity is included; it sends the point at infinity to the point at infinity and an affine point $(x, y)$ to $(u^2 x + r,\ u^3 y + u^2 s x + t)$.

results.title: Variable changes preserve the point count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $W$ be an elliptic Weierstrass curve over a finite field $F$, let $C$ be a variable change and let $C \cdot W$ be the transformed curve. Then $C \cdot W$ and $W$ have the same number of rational points.

results.title: The ideal of a point on a Weierstrass curve is nonzero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The ideal generated by `X - x` and `Y - y` is nonzero.

results.title: Geometrically reduced variety over a field
results.caption: Class
results.summary: Let $k$ be a field. A scheme $X$ with a chosen structure morphism $X \to \operatorname{Spec} k$ is a *variety* over $k$ if this morphism is separated, of finite type (quasi-compact and locally of finite type), and geometrically reduced.

results.title: Characterization of varieties
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme with a structure morphism $X \to \operatorname{Spec} k$. Then $X$ is a variety over $k$ if and only if this structure morphism is separated, locally of finite type, quasi-compact and geometrically reduced.

results.title: Varieties are quasi-separated
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $X$ is a variety over a field $k$, then its structure morphism $X \to \operatorname{Spec} k$ is quasi-separated, since it is separated.

results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A separable data matrix: columns `m j` are sub-convex combinations of `r` linearly independent archetypes `w k`, and every archetype is a column (Gillis–Vavasis Assumption 1).

results.title: Residual of a column in the successive projection algorithm
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Run of the successive projection algorithm
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: `S` (most recent pick first) is a run of the successive projection algorithm: each pick maximizes the residual norm given the earlier picks (ties broken arbitrarily).

results.title: Norm bound for a sub-convex combination of vectors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Gillis–Vavasis Lemma 1 (`f = ‖·‖²`), bound: a sub-convex combination of vectors of norm at most `M` has norm at most `M`.

results.title: Equality case of the sub-convex combination norm bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Gillis–Vavasis Lemma 1 (`f = ‖·‖²`), equality case: for linearly independent vectors of norm at most `M > 0`, a sub-convex combination of norm `M` is a vertex `w k` with `‖w k‖ = M`.

results.title: Vertex cover scan
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a finite set $C$ of vertices and a list of pairs of vertices, the scan processes the pairs in order, starting from the cover $C$ and charging one time unit per pair. A pair $(u, v)$ is covered when $u$ or $v$ is already in the current cover; a covered pair is skipped, and an uncovered pair adds both $u$ and $v$ to the cover. The scan returns the cover reached after the last pair.

results.title: APPROX-VERTEX-COVER
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a list $L$ of ordered pairs of vertices, APPROX-VERTEX-COVER starts from the empty cover and goes through $L$ in order: a pair $(u, v)$ with $u$ or $v$ already in the cover is skipped, and otherwise both $u$ and $v$ are added to the cover. It returns the final cover, a finite set of vertices, at a cost of one unit per pair of $L$.

results.title: Running time of the vertex cover scan
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite set $C$ of vertices and every list $L$ of pairs of vertices, the running time of the vertex cover scan starting from $C$ on $L$ is the length of $L$.

results.title: Running time of APPROX-VERTEX-COVER
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $L$ of ordered pairs of vertices, the cost of APPROX-VERTEX-COVER on $L$ is the length of $L$: one unit per listed pair.

results.title: The vertex cover scan only adds vertices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite set $C$ of vertices and every list of pairs of vertices, the cover returned by the vertex cover scan starting from $C$ on that list contains $C$.

results.title: APPROX-VERTEX-COVER covers every listed pair
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $L$ of ordered pairs of vertices and every pair $(u, v)$ in $L$, the cover that APPROX-VERTEX-COVER returns on $L$ contains $u$ or $v$.

results.title: APPROX-VERTEX-COVER returns a vertex cover
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph and $L$ a list of ordered pairs of vertices such that for every edge $uv$ of $G$, $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ is in $L$. Then the cover that APPROX-VERTEX-COVER returns on $L$ is a vertex cover of $G$.

results.title: Counting invariant of the vertex cover scan
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph, $S$ a vertex cover of $G$, $C_0$ a finite set of vertices with $|C_0| \le 2|C_0 \cap S|$, and $L$ a list of ordered pairs of vertices such that $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G$ for every $(u, v)$ in $L$. Then the cover $C$ that the vertex cover scan returns on $L$ starting from $C_0$ satisfies $|C| \le 2|C \cap S|$.

results.title: APPROX-VERTEX-COVER is at most twice any vertex cover
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph and $L$ a list of ordered pairs of vertices such that $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G$ for every $(u, v)$ in $L$. Then for every vertex cover $S$ of $G$, finite or infinite, the cover $C$ that APPROX-VERTEX-COVER returns on $L$ satisfies $|C| \le 2|S|$, with sizes in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$.

results.title: APPROX-VERTEX-COVER is a 2-approximation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph and $L$ a list of ordered pairs of vertices that lists exactly the edges of $G$, each in at least one orientation: $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G$ for every $(u, v)$ in $L$, and for every edge $uv$ of $G$, $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ is in $L$. Then the cover $C$ that APPROX-VERTEX-COVER returns on $L$ is a vertex cover of $G$ and $|C| \le 2\tau(G)$, where $\tau(G) \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$…

part.title: String matching problem
api: A pattern occurs in a text iff it matches at some offset

results.title: Pattern match at an offset
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For lists $p$ (the pattern) and $t$ (the text) over a type $\alpha$ and a natural number $k$, the pattern $p$ matches the text $t$ at the zero-based offset $k$ when $k$ is at most the length of $t$ and $p$ is a prefix of the list obtained from $t$ by dropping its first $k$ entries.

results.title: Characterization of a match at an offset
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For lists $p$ and $t$ and a natural number $k$, the pattern $p$ matches the text $t$ at the zero-based offset $k$ if and only if $k$ is at most the length of $t$ and $p$ is a prefix of the list obtained from $t$ by dropping its first $k$ entries.

results.title: A pattern occurs in a text iff it matches at some offset
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For lists $p$ and $t$, there is an offset $k$ such that the pattern $p$ matches the text $t$ at $k$ if and only if $p$ is an infix of $t$, that is, $t$ is the concatenation of some list $u$, then $p$, then some list $v$.

results.title: Mean fitness of a population state
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mean fitness `f̄(x) = ∑ i, x i * f x i` of the population state `x` for the fitness function `f`.

results.title: Solution of the replicator equation
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: `x` solves the replicator equation `x_i' = x_i (f_i(x) - f̄(x))` for all times `t ≥ 0`.

results.title: Rest point of the replicator equation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: `x` is a rest point of the replicator equation: `x_i (f_i(x) - f̄(x)) = 0` for all `i`.

results.title: Rest points in the interior are equalizers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If every strategy is present (`x i > 0`), then `x` is a rest point iff every strategy has fitness equal to the mean fitness.

results.title: Evolution of the total frequency under replicator dynamics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The total frequency `∑ x_i` evolves by `(∑ x_i)' = f̄(x) (1 - ∑ x_i)`.

results.title: Invariance of the simplex hyperplane
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For continuous fitness `f`, a solution with `∑ x_i(0) = 1` satisfies `∑ x_i(t) = 1` for all `t ≥ 0`.

results.title: Invariance of the faces of the simplex
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For continuous fitness `f`, a strategy absent at time `0` (`x_i(0) = 0`) stays absent for all `t ≥ 0`.

results.title: Present strategies stay present
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For continuous fitness `f`, a strategy with positive frequency at time `0` has positive frequency for all `t ≥ 0`.

results.title: Invariance of the simplex (Hofbauer–Sigmund 1998, §7.1)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For continuous fitness `f`, a solution starting in the standard simplex (`x i ≥ 0` for all `i` and `∑ i, x i = 1`) stays in it for all `t ≥ 0`.
